newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Little room seen for Brazil spread tightening.
newsitem.headline: Little room seen for Brazil spread tightening.

text.p: Brazilian Eurobond spreads, which have narrowed sharply in recent weeks on positive local news and a strong appetite for emerging market paper, should consolidate at current levels, traders and analysts said.
"They've hit a consolidation level at this point. We see room for further tightening but not until we get more progress on re-election," said a trader at a leading foreign bank in Brazil.
Brazilian spreads have tightened by an average of about 30 basis points over the past two weeks in secondary market Eurobond trading.

Much of the gain has been attributed to healthy investor demand for Latin American paper, which has also boosted Mexican and Argentine Eurobonds. But Brazil's strong performance was also seen tied to anticipation of congressional support for a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election in 1998.
While Cardoso won a first round vote in the lower house this week, traders said his fight for re-election isn't over yet.

"All the good news is not in yet. They still have to get through internal congressional elections, a second round of voting on re-election in the lower house and then two votes in the Senate," said another trader in Brazil who requested anonymity.
Top rank Brazilian banks have led corporate issuers into record tight spread territory over the past two weeks.

Following successful three-year dollar deals by Bradesco and Unibanco - both of which priced at 190 bps over and quickly traded up to 170 bps over - the market began speculating that Itau's expected new issue would price at 170 bps over.
But many Brazil debt watchers questioned whether Itau could come in at such a pricey spread.
"We've seen three-year bank issues coming in at 190 over but I would be surprised if they come in lower than that," said Claudio Prado, a salesman for West Merchant Bank in New York.
"I think a lot of the good news this week was anticipated and I would be surprised if in the following weeks we're going to see further tightening," Prado said.

Brazilian Eurobonds have followed upward price movements in Bradys over the past few weeks. But debt watchers said any downturn in the U.S. Treasury market might hit Bradys harder than Eurobonds because there was stiff competition to lead manage Brazilian Eurobond deals, which would keep launch prices on the expensive side.
